title: Enteric methane mitigation that farmers will use
bottleneck: Ruminant methane is a huge climate lever — Asparagopsis seaweed cuts emissions up to 80% in trials — but practical deployment is stuck: additives must be fed daily, dosing in grazing systems is near-impossible, seaweed supply doesn't exist at scale, and farmers get no payment for the reduction. The science works in feedlots; the world's cattle mostly graze. Additives must be fed daily, dosing in grazing systems is near-impossible, and farmers get no payment for the reduction.
why_it_blocks: Livestock methane is ~30% of anthropogenic methane. A solution that only works in controlled feedlots leaves most emissions untouched.
current_state: 3-NOP (Bovaer) is approved in multiple countries for feedlot use; grazing-compatible delivery and scaled supply chains are unsolved.

sources.title: A comprehensive review of livestock methane emissions: emission factors, quantification methods, and mitigation strategies
